chunks: And from him, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Mu'awiya ibn Wahb, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): Did the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) say, 'What is between my pulpit and my house is a garden from the gardens of Paradise?' He said, 'Yes.'
And he said, 'The house of Ali and Fatimah (peace be upon her) is what is between the house in which the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) is, to the door that faces the alley, to al-Baqi'.'
He said, 'If you entered from that door, with the wall in its place, your left shoulder would touch it; then he named the other houses.'
And he said, 'The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said,

key_terms.رَوْضَةٌ: A garden or meadow, metaphorically used for a blessed place

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual significance of the area between the Prophet's pulpit and his house according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* underscores the spiritual geography of Medina by equating the space between the Prophet’s pulpit and home with a garden of Paradise, while simultaneously defining the precise boundaries of the Ahl al-Bayt’s residence to affirm their unique status. It concludes by reinforcing the merit of congregational prayer in the Prophet’s Mosque, noting its equivalence to a thousand prayers elsewhere, a virtue second only to the Sacred Mosque. This narration serves as a key textual basis for the reverence of the Prophet’s domestic space and the elevated rank of the Imams within it.
